title: Demand Curator: regional routing policy with latency smoothing, staged pinning, and capacity grace
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Sudden regional capacity pressure and transient network flaps cause abrupt failovers that spike tail latency, exhaust KV cache locality benefits, and trigger waterfall retries across regions. Current routing decisions are binary (pin/unpin) or immediate hedges that cause oscillation and poor SLO behavior for latency-sensitive tenants.

Goal: Implement a routing layer called 'Demand Curator' that smooths latency signals, applies staged geo-pinning with probabilistic decay, and uses per-region capacity grace tokens to permit controlled soft spillback. The policy should reduce p95 tail spikes during failovers, preserve KV cache locality where possible, and bound cross-region traffic during sustained overloads.

Non-goals: Full autoscaling policy changes (this work assumes existing autoscalers), work on dedicated pricing or billing changes, and modifications to model selection logic beyond routing decisions.
design:
Summary: Demand Curator is a decision service that sits between the request director and the region dispatch layer. It consumes per-region telemetry (latency quantiles, util, queue depth), maintains short and mid-term smoothed signals, and outputs a routing score per region. Scores drive three actions: allow (route), soft-pin (prefer local unless score drops below spill threshold), and probabilistic spill (sample remote regions).

Key differentiators vs. current approaches:
- Latency smoothing uses dual-window EWMA (fast window for spikes, slow window for trend) computed on p50/p95/p99 separately.
- Staged pinning: when local region degrades, we move from allow -> soft-pin (decayable) -> unpin. Soft-pin allows bounded fraction of requests to spill to remote to preserve cache/locality for most traffic.
- Capacity grace tokens: each region maintains a small token escrow that permits short bursts above nominal capacity; token refill is proportional to observed spare capacity and decays during sustained pressure. Tokens are 'consumed' per-request via token weight heuristics (longer seqs cost more).
- Two-tier circuit breakers: fast trip (short-term spikes) halts new hedges for 1-3s to avoid oscillation; slow trip (sustained overload) reduces admission with progressive shed rates and engages emergency spill policy.

Routing score components (weighted):
- Smoothed latency penalty (p95 normalized to SLO target)
- Capacity headroom score (free tokens / token cap)
- Queue depth pressure (exponential penalty beyond threshold)
- Regional priority override (customer pinning preferences)
algorithm_steps: 1) Ingest per-region telemetry every 1s: p50/p95/p99, utilization, avg request token cost, queue depth.
2) Compute EWMA-fast (alpha_f = 0.4) and EWMA-slow (alpha_s = 0.05) for p95 and p99. Combine into composite latency_score = 0.7 * EWMA-fast + 0.3 * EWMA-slow.
3) Normalize latency_score against region SLO target to produce latency_penalty in 0..1 range.
4) Compute token_escrow_ratio = available_tokens / max_tokens (max_tokens proportional to region capacity).
6) routing_score = w_latency*latency_penalty + w_capacity*(1 - token_escrow_ratio) + w_queue*queue_penalty - priority_override.

7) Decision logic: if routing_score < allow_threshold -> route normally; if allow_threshold <= score < soft_pin_threshold -> mark request soft-pin (route locally with X% spill); if soft_pin_threshold <= score < spill_threshold -> probabilistic spill to remote with probability p(score); if score >= circuit_breaker_threshold -> engage circuit-breaker (reject or route to degraded path).

8) Token consumption: each routed request deducts token_weight = base_weight * (1 + seq_len_factor). If tokens exhausted, region token_escrow_ratio falls and routing_score increases, triggering spillback.

9) Circuit-breakers: fast-trip uses 5s sliding window on p99 spikes; slow-trip uses 2m sustained util > 95% with high queue_depth. Fast-trip pauses new remote hedges for 1-3s; slow-trip increases shed_rate progressively up to 30% and notifies Ops channel.
10) Decay/unpin: soft-pins have a probabilistic decay every 10s: pinned_fraction *= 0.95 + small_random_noise to avoid synchronized unpinning.
11) Fallbacks: if external region fails to accept traffic, controller retries with backoff and increases local token escrow donation if allowed.
12) Telemetry emitted per decision: decision_id, chosen_region, upstream_score, tokens_before_after, pin_state, shed_decision, reason_code.
13) Backpressure to client: when shedding, respond with explicit error codes and Retry-After headers where applicable; track per-customer degradations for SLA accounting.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Under controlled single-region outage test, p95 for affected tenants increases by no more than 30% compared to baseline while overall p99 remains within 2x baseline for less than 60s.

A2: During a sustained capacity reduction (50% capacity for 3 minutes), cross-region spill traffic should ramp smoothly (no >3x sudden spikes) and KV cache locality retained for >=65% of requests compared to baseline.
A3: Circuit-breaker fast-trip reduces oscillation: measured flip-flop rate of pin/unpin < 1 per minute per region under injected jitter.
A4: Shed rate under emergency slow-trip stays below configured cap (30%) and customer-impacted error rate is recorded and surfaced to Console's SLO dashboard.
A5: Unit and integration tests for routing_score math, token accounting, and decay behavior exist and pass in CI; canary in one region for 48h without critical alerts.
A6: Telemetry described in telemetry_metrics is available in dashboards and can be exported to long-term metrics store for analysis.
test_plan: Unit tests: EWMA math, token account edge cases, routing_score thresholds.
Integration: end-to-end director -> curator -> dispatcher path using a simulator with synthetic telemetry (fail/restore, latency spikes, gradual capacity drain).
Chaos: induce transient network partition for 30s and measure p95/p99 and KV hit rate changes.
Load: 1.5x production poisson load for 10 minutes with injected regional capacity drop to validate soft-spill behavior.
Canary rollout: 1% of traffic in non-critical region for 24h, then 10% for 48h with ops playbook rehearsed.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Canary in staging with simulated multi-region telemetry. Phase 1: 1% traffic in non-critical region for 24h (monitoring & safety kill). Phase 2: 10% traffic in two pilot regions for 48h with ops on-call. Phase 3: Global gradual ramp by traffic slices (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) with 2h observation windows. Emergency rollback: toggle feature-flag to fallback to current binary pin policy. Post-rollout: 7-day observation window to compare SLO delta and update defaults.
notes: We must coordinate with Dedicated team to ensure token_escrow max_tokens calculation aligns with reserved capacity reporting. Also confirm that Console can surface per-customer shed metrics before canary. Consider a tuning pass to adjust token weights by model type (embedding vs. generation).
